not_covered: Fish counts. No licensed source yet, so the fishing view shows where the water matches each species, not how many fish are there.
Bait at barges other than Everingham's three (Oceanside, Newport, San Pedro, Redondo, Marina del Rey): they post by phone or social media, so only reports from the water cover them.
Current at dive depth. HF radar measures the surface only and is blank within about 1.5 miles of shore.
Beach water-quality notices. San Diego County's beach status site has no public data feed; connecting it needs a feed from the county.
The thermocline at the kelp. The observed profile comes from a glider offshore; the SCCOOS Del Mar kelp mooring did not answer when this was built.
Boats without AIS (most under 65 ft), and Mexican waters beyond shore-receiver range.

species.label: Bluefin tuna
species.note: Sport-fleet catch peaks at 63-70°F (Runcie 2019); in warmer surface water bluefin go deep, out of reach of surface gear.

species.label: Yellowfin tuna
species.note: Holds on the warm, clear side of fronts (Block 1997); a shallow mixed layer pushes it up.

species.label: Dorado (mahi)
species.note: The paddy fish: 75% of Mexican Pacific catch at chlorophyll 0.05-0.25 mg/m³ (Marín-Enríquez 2018).

species.label: Yellowtail (offshore, paddy fish)
species.note: San Diego catch rates rise at 64-68°F and fall above 69°F (Squire 1982; inshore fleet data).

species.label: Striped marlin
species.note: San Diego catch averaged 67.8°F; works breaks and blue water against green over the banks.

species.label: Wahoo
species.note: A warm-year visitor (CPFV: 42 in 2014, 256 in 2015); holds on banks and high spots.

fleet_recent.coverage_note: AIS is heard only within roughly 30-50 nm of shore receivers, and most boats under 65 ft never broadcast it.

inshore.label: Yellowtail (islands and kelp)
inshore.drivers: Warm-year regime (landings swing from under 10,000 to 450,000 fish), bait: squid, sardine, mackerel.
inshore.look: Outer kelp edge next to deep water, up-current points at the islands.
inshore.evidence: Strong for the regime; the 64-66°F 'switch' is angler lore.
inshore.today: Surface water is 74°F; San Diego catch rates have fallen above 69°F in fleet data.

inshore.label: White seabass
inshore.drivers: Spawning Mar-Jul (peak May); tagged fish spent half their time at 55-61°F, tracking the thermocline.
inshore.look: Kelp near squid grounds, at dusk; near the surface Apr-Oct, deeper Dec-Feb.
inshore.evidence: Thermal niche from one tagging study (Aalbers & Sepulveda 2015).
inshore.today: Surface water is 74°F, above the 55-61°F the tagged fish used; the cooler water they favored sits below the thermocline.

inshore.label: Calico (kelp) bass
inshore.drivers: Small home ranges; spawns Jun-Aug at 25-60 ft under kelp.

inshore.label: Market squid (the bait that drives the inshore bite)
inshore.drivers: Landings crash after big El Niños; eggs at 50-58°F.
inshore.evidence: Strong for the El Niño effect: a weak squid year is likely this winter.

fishing.method: Profiles say where the water matches what each species needs, not how many fish are there. Water temperature is the satellite map's; breaks are the strongest gradient within 10 nm of a spot, read as the temperature change across 4.3 nm. A cue met at most in-range spots that day is 'everywhere' and singles nothing out.
fishing.counts_note: No dock counts: the network that publishes SoCal landing counts now forbids automated collection and republishing without a license.

bottom_line: Shore diving today: outside our thresholds at La Jolla Cove, La Jolla Shores, Point Loma and Sunset Cliffs, and Laguna Beach. The San Diego County surf forecast is 2 to 4 feet, sets to 5 feet from 210°, with a moderate rip current risk.

By boat today: marginal for the Coronados, the offshore banks and the outer islands; within our thresholds for San Diego inshore and Catalina and the San Pedro Channel. Friday gets worse for Catalina and the San Pedro Channel and the outer islands (wind, seas and steep short-period chop).
Nearshore buoys read 73-75°F as of 7:56 PM; the latest satellite temperature map is from Oct 19.

fishing: By boat today: marginal for the Coronados, the offshore banks and the outer islands; within our thresholds for San Diego inshore and Catalina and the San Pedro Channel. Friday gets worse for Catalina and the San Pedro Channel and the outer islands (wind, seas and steep short-period chop).
Water at the named spots runs 68-75°F on the Oct 19 satellite map; the strongest break is near Cortes Bank, 2.3°F over 4.3 nm, warm side to the SE.
Season and water both match today for bluefin tuna, yellowfin tuna, dorado, yellowtail, striped marlin and wahoo. That says the water is right, not that fish are there.

synopsis.text: At 2 PM, a 1011 mb low was just north of the Bay Area, a 1007 mb low was over the Nevada/Utah border and a 1026 mb high was about 1270 nautical miles west of San Diego. A storm system continues to move through the coastal waters today through Friday. There is a slight chance of thunderstorms this afternoon. Any thunderstorm is capable of producing gusty, erratic winds, choppy seas, lightning, briefly heavy rainfall with reduced visibility, and waterspouts. Isolated northwest wind gusts will occasionally exceed 20 knots on Friday. Weak offshore flow during the nights and mornings will alternate with onshore northwest flow during the afternoons and evenings for Friday night through Monday.

At 20Z or 1 PM PDT, there was a 1007 mb surface low centered over southwestern Idaho with a cold front extending S of the low through AZ and Baja. There was also a 1011 mb surface low along the Central CA coast with a trough of low pressure extending S of the low. A slight chance of thunderstorms will continue this afternoon for the southern coastal waters.

headlines.description:
* WHAT...Hazardous sea conditions.

* WHERE...Outer waters from Santa Cruz Island to San Clemente
Island to 60 NM offshore including San Nicolas and Santa
Barbara Islands.

* WHEN...From 6 AM Friday to 3 AM PDT Saturday.

* IMPACTS...Conditions will be hazardous to small craft.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...See the Coastal Waters Forecast (CWFLOX)
for more.
headlines.instruction:
Inexperienced mariners, especially those operating smaller
vessels, should avoid navigating in hazardous conditions.

fishing: Since Oct 13, water warmed in 11 zones and cooled in 0; the biggest move was Rockpile / Upper 500 (+2.2°F). Warmest: Rockpile / Upper 500 at 74.7°F; coolest: Tanner / Cortes at 68.3°F.
Strongest offshore break: Tanner / Cortes, 2.3°F over 4.3 nm at 32 28 x 118 58, warm side SE. It has softened over the last three map days.
The paddy drift model's core regions sit in San Clemente Is., 9 Mile / 43, Tanner / Cortes, South 9 / 302 / 425 and Rockpile / Upper 500.

AIS-tracked boats stopped longest in 14 Mile / Avalon Bank over the last three days (0.2 h). The same weeks last year, the fleet's stops concentrated at Tanner / Cortes (140 h), 14 Mile / Avalon Bank (38 h) and Rockpile / Upper 500 (25 h).
